clue.text: Cloth showing a couple of male creatures

parts.note: a buck is a male deer or rabbit, the first of the pair
a ram is a male sheep, the second of the pair

explanation.surface: A piece of material depicts two male animals.
explanation.walkthrough: The one phrase supplies two pieces: two different male animals placed side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Buckram is a stiffened coarse cotton or linen used in bookbinding and tailoring.

clue.text: A lot of big noises appearing heartless

indicators.note: means without its heart, so the central letter is removed

parts.note: bangs are loud noises

explanation.surface: Many important people are shown to be unfeeling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'big noises' suggests VIPs, but it means loud bangs; 'heartless' drops the middle N.
explanation.definitionFit: Bags is informal British for plenty, as in 'bags of time'.

clue.text: It provides new energy for horse

definitions.meaning: a device that recharges a battery
a war horse, the mount of a knight

explanation.surface: Something gives a fresh boost to a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A charger is both a battery-recharging device and a cavalry mount.

clue.text: Give notice when ousting second in command

indicators.note: means throwing out, so a letter is removed from the first word

parts.note: to resign is to give notice of leaving a job

explanation.surface: A deputy leader hands in their notice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second in command' reads as a deputy, but 'in' is a link and 'command' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Reign is the exercise of sovereign power, rule or command over a realm.

clue.text: Current help to traditional wheels of industry

definitions.text: Current help to traditional wheels of industry

parts.words: Current help to traditional wheels of industry
parts.note: a flow of water channelled to drive the waterwheel of an old grinding works

explanation.surface: Present-day assistance for old established industrial firms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' looks like 'present-day' and 'wheels of industry' like big businesses; read them literally, as moving water and waterwheels.
explanation.definitionFit: A millrace is the channel of fast water that turns a mill's waterwheel.

clue.text: Good relations offering chat and wine

parts.note: to rap is an informal word for to talk or chat
port is a fortified wine from Portugal

explanation.surface: Friendly ties are built over conversation and a glass of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapport is a harmonious understanding between people, a close and sympathetic connection.

clue.text: Whisper coming from good man in control

indicators.note: puts the saint inside the word for control

parts.note: rule means control
ST is short for saint, a good man

explanation.surface: A rumour emerges from a decent man in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: A rustle is a soft, murmuring sound like leaves or a whisper.

clue.text: Lying sort, loose in chatter

indicators.note: puts the jumbled letters inside the word for chatter

parts.note: to prate is to chatter foolishly

indicators.note: loose means not tightly bound, so these letters come apart and rearrange

explanation.surface: A dishonest kind of person, careless in gossip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lying' means stretched out flat, not fibbing; 'loose' jumbles the four letters into OSTR, set inside the chatter word.
explanation.definitionFit: Prostrate means lying stretched out face down on the ground.

clue.text: Actor is one in more demanding title role

indicators.note: puts the numeral inside the role's name

parts.note: Oliver Twist, title character of Dickens's novel, famously asks for more
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A performer plays a pushier leading part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'more demanding' recalls Oliver Twist asking for more gruel. Laurence Olivier was a great English stage and screen actor.
explanation.definitionFit: Laurence Olivier was one of the most celebrated actors of the twentieth century.

clue.text: Batsman coming in first wicker down to knock up 60

parts.words: Batsman coming in first wicker down
parts.note: in cricket the number three batsman comes in when the first wicket falls
to knock up runs is to score them

explanation.surface: A batsman arrives at the fall of the first wicket and makes sixty.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a wicket 'down' is a batsman out; the third in the order comes in after the first one is out.
explanation.definitionFit: Threescore is an old word for sixty, three twenties.

clue.text: Flowering plant makes one tortured soul pleased at first

indicators.note: says that this piece comes at the front of the whole answer

parts.note: glad means pleased
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: something tortured is twisted out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A garden bloom is said to cheer up a suffering spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tortured' turns SOUL into OLUS; 'at first' puts GLAD ahead of I and OLUS.
explanation.definitionFit: The gladiolus is a garden plant with tall spikes of brightly coloured flowers.

clue.text: Branch of bank used by craftsman

definitions.text: Branch of bank used by craftsman

parts.words: Branch of bank used by craftsman
parts.note: reads like a financial institution's local office, but means a willow shoot growing beside a river, cut by a basket-maker

explanation.surface: A local bank office is patronised by an artisan.
explanation.walkthrough: The financial sense of 'branch' and 'bank' is the misdirection: think of a riverbank tree and a basket-weaver.
explanation.definitionFit: Osiers are willow twigs, grown on wet riverside ground and woven into baskets and wicker.

clue.text: Officer's threewheeler coming to complete stop

parts.note: a general is a senior army officer; the possessive gives the S
a trike is a tricycle, a vehicle with three wheels

explanation.surface: A commander's tricycle is brought to a halt.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive S is part of the answer here. A general strike is a stoppage of work by all trades at once, as in Britain in 1926.
explanation.definitionFit: A general strike halts work across the whole economy, a total stoppage of labour.

clue.text: Pat's the ref, silly old man who's replaced another

indicators.note: silly means foolish or scrambled-headed, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A football fan grumbles that Pat, the referee, is foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'silly' rearranges the letters of PATS THE REF; 'old man' is slang for father.
explanation.definitionFit: A stepfather is a mother's later husband, taking the place of the birth father.

clue.text: Performance in town again? Start heading for home

parts.note: a turn is a short act or performance, as in a variety show
someone who has returned to town is back

explanation.surface: A touring act is in town once more, then sets off homeward.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark suggests a returning show, but it splits into two pieces, an act and being returned.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn back is to reverse direction and go back towards where one started.

clue.text: Nothing to be pat in vessel on river-it may be kept in this

definitions.text: it may be kept in this

indicators.note: says the zero goes inside the vessel word

parts.note: a bath is a vessel holding water
O, the figure zero, means nothing
the Ouse is an English river

explanation.surface: Nothing is to be loaded on a river boat, which may be stored in here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' refers back to the river vessel: a boat is kept in this. 'on' is a link meaning followed by.
explanation.definitionFit: A boathouse is a shed by the water where boats are stored.

clue.text: Material used in roof-a brick

indicators.note: says the letters needed are found inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Something goes into the roofing along with a brick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used in' points at the letters straddling 'roof-a brick'.
explanation.definitionFit: Fabric is cloth or textile, and also more broadly the material a building is made of.

clue.text: Demonstration disrupting most profound political initiative

indicators.note: means breaking into, so the march goes into the middle of the other word
means nearly all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: deep means profound
a march is a protest demonstration

explanation.surface: A protest wrecks a very serious policy move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most profound' reads as a superlative, but 'most' takes all but the last letter of DEEP, giving DEE, which MARCH breaks into.
explanation.definitionFit: A démarche is a diplomatic step or political move, often a formal protest.

clue.text: Drama when areas dried up

parts.note: a play is a drama
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: A play is staged while the land around it has turned dry.
explanation.definitionFit: Playas are dry, flat beds of desert lakes that hold water only after rain.

clue.text: Aerial insect has upset girl!

parts.note: an ant is an insect

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the girl's name is read upwards

parts.note: Anne is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl is distressed by a creepy-crawly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Aerial' looks like an adjective, but it is the noun for a radio rod. 'upset' turns ANNE into ENNA.
explanation.definitionFit: An antenna is a radio aerial, and also an insect's feeler.

clue.text: Academic session makes one seem troubled, needing rest somehow

indicators.note: something troubled is disturbed, so these letters are mixed up
means in some unspecified way, so these letters are put in another order

explanation.surface: A term at college leaves a student looking worried and in need of a break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troubled' rearranges SEEM to SEME and 'somehow' rearranges REST to STER.
explanation.definitionFit: A semester is a half-year term in a college or university calendar.

clue.text: Where drivers may have to pull up in worst possible situation

definitions.text: Where drivers may have to pull up
definitions.meaning: the service bays beside a motor-racing track

explanation.surface: Racing drivers forced to stop find themselves in dire straits.
explanation.definitionFit: In motor racing, cars stop at the side lanes; colloquially the phrase means something awful.

clue.text: Liveliness as priest brings French art to the fore

indicators.note: with 'to the fore', says a run of letters is moved to the front of the word

parts.note: es is French for '(thou) art', the old form of 'are'

explanation.surface: A clergyman's energy draws French painting to prominence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brings ... to the fore' moves ES to the front of PRIEST; 'art' is the verb, as in 'thou art', not painting.
explanation.definitionFit: Esprit means wit and liveliness of mind.

clue.text: Inanimate, treated with this drug

indicators.note: something treated has been worked on or processed, so these letters are reorganised

explanation.surface: A lifeless thing is dosed with this medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treated' shuffles INANIMATE together with THIS.
explanation.definitionFit: An antihistamine is a medicine that counters allergic reactions such as hay fever.

clue.text: One style of architecture I love — pleasant, not English

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written O

indicators.note: means without, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: nice means pleasant

explanation.surface: An admirer of classical buildings finds them agreeable, though not English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'love' is a tennis score of nil, the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Ionic is one of the classical orders of columns, with scroll-shaped capitals.

clue.text: Vassal's land producing lengthy quarrel

definitions.meaning: a feudal estate held in return for service, a fief

explanation.surface: A tenant's estate leads to a long dispute.
explanation.definitionFit: A feud is a fief in feudal law and also a prolonged hostility between families.

clue.text: As religious type, back superior

parts.note: hind means at the back, as in hind legs
U stands for upper-class, a superior social register

explanation.surface: A believer is said to support someone of higher standing.
explanation.walkthrough: U meaning upper-class, as opposed to non-U, is an old British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hindu is a follower of Hinduism, the main faith of India.

clue.text: Obscure ceremony outside city on first of December

indicators.note: says the ceremony word goes round the other pieces

parts.note: a rite is a ritual ceremony
EC is the postcode of the City of London
taken as written

indicators.note: takes the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A mysterious ritual takes place outside the city on the first of the month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' has the ceremony word wrap the rest; 'city' means the City of London, London's financial district, whose postcode letters are a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: Recondite means little known or abstruse, understood only by a few specialists.

clue.text: Opening time restricted — that'll produce a reaction

indicators.note: says the first word confines the other within its letters

parts.note: a rent is a tear or opening
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Limited opening hours provoke a response.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opening' is not a time of day but a rip, RENT, which holds AGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A reagent is a substance added in chemistry to bring about a reaction.

clue.text: Former copper starts to sue evildoer dubiously given pardon

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: takes the opening letter of each of the next three words

explanation.surface: An ex-policeman starts suing a criminal, who is doubtfully let off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a police officer but is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Excused means forgiven or let off, released from blame.
